# AEVIS

Measurement and governance platform for RAG systems. Specs: `docs/superpowers/specs/`; MVP roadmap: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-15-aevis-mvp-roadmap.md`.

## Run locally

    docker compose -f deploy/docker-compose.yml up --build -d
    docker compose -f deploy/docker-compose.yml run --rm api aevis admin bootstrap --tenant-name <name> --admin-username <user>

Open http://localhost:8080 and sign in with the printed one-time password.

## Develop

- Backend: `cd backend && uv sync && uv run pytest` (Docker needed for `tests/integration`).
- Web: `cd web && pnpm install && pnpm dev` (proxies `/api` to `localhost:8000`). After API changes, run `pnpm gen:api`.

# React + TypeScript + Vite

This template provides a minimal setup to get React working in Vite with HMR and some Oxlint rules.

Currently, two official plugins are available:

- [@vitejs/plugin-react](https://github.com/vitejs/vite-plugin-react/blob/main/packages/plugin-react) uses [Oxc](https://oxc.rs)
- [@vitejs/plugin-react-swc](https://github.com/vitejs/vite-plugin-react/blob/main/packages/plugin-react-swc) uses [SWC](https://swc.rs/)

## React Compiler

The React Compiler is not enabled on this template because of its impact on dev & build performances. To add it, see [this documentation](https://react.dev/learn/react-compiler/installation).

## Expanding the Oxlint configuration

If you are developing a production application, we recommend enabling type-aware lint rules by installing `oxlint-tsgolint` and editing `.oxlintrc.json`:

```json
{
  "$schema": "./node_modules/oxlint/configuration_schema.json",
  "plugins": ["react", "typescript", "oxc"],
  "options": {
    "typeAware": true
  },
  "rules": {
    "react/rules-of-hooks": "error",
    "react/only-export-components": ["warn", { "allowConstantExport": true }]
  }
}
```

See the [Oxlint rules documentation](https://oxc.rs/docs/guide/usage/linter/rules) for the full list of rules and categories.

simreadme.text:
# aevis-sim

A deterministic simulated RAG endpoint (Step 1 spec §6). It plays an external system, so it
imports nothing from `aevis`, and it answers in its own JSON shape. AEVIS maps that shape with
JSONPath, exactly as it would for a real endpoint.

Pipeline: PyMuPDF extraction → chunker (`fixed-256` or `recursive-512`) → BM25 → an extractive
answer from the top chunks. It abstains when nothing matches well enough.

```bash
uv --directory sim run uvicorn aevis_sim.app:app --port 8090
curl -s localhost:8090/v1/ask -H 'X-Sim-Profile: instrumented' \
  -d '{"id":"q1","q":"What is the standard mileage rate?","k":5}' -H 'content-type: application/json'
```

## Request headers

| Header | Values | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `X-Sim-Profile` | `core`, `core_text` (default), `with_context`, `instrumented`, `temporal`, `no_candidates` | Picks which fields the response includes |
| `X-Sim-Faults` | comma list: `latency:<ms>`, `timeout:<rate>`, `rate_limit:<rate>`, `malformed:<rate>`, `drop_declared:<capability>`, `bad_context_id:<rate>`, `uncited:<rate>`, `drift:prior_edition`, `ignore_as_of` | Injects failures, seeded by `(seed, id)` so they reproduce |
| `X-Sim-Chunker` | `fixed-256` (default), `recursive-512` | Picks the chunker |
| `X-Sim-Seed` | int | Seed for the faults |
| `X-AEVIS-Idempotency-Key` | any string | A repeated key returns the cached response and is listed at `GET /v1/duplicates` |
| `X-AEVIS-Attempt` | `1`, `2`, … | Attempt 1 (or no header) draws faults by query id; a later attempt draws them afresh, so a retry can succeed |

The `temporal` profile honours `as_of` and `question_time` in the body. It serves, for each
document, the latest edition that was ingested (or valid) by that date. Dates are set in
`corpus/manifest.yaml`.

`GET /v1/stats` returns `{"requests", "max_in_flight"}` (the most calls served at once); `POST /v1/stats/reset` zeroes it and the idempotency log.

# AEVIS MVP milestones

One file per lifecycle step. Each one says how to deploy that step on your machine, what to click, and what you should see. A step is signed off when every box in its sign-off checklist is ticked.

| Step | What it delivers | Branch | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | [Foundation](step-00-foundation.md): sign-in, users, the workspace shell, the platform services | `feat/mvp-01-foundation` (PR #31) | Signed off 2026-10-17 |
| 1 | [Project and target](step-01-project-and-target.md): projects, roles, the target wizard and probe, approval, preflight | `feat/mvp-02-project-target` (PR #32) | Merged |
| 2 | [Corpus and evidence](step-02-corpus.md): corpus snapshots, PDF extraction, evidence import, span mapping | `feat/mvp-03-corpus` (PR #34) | Signed off 2026-10-18 |
| 3 | [Benchmark](step-03-benchmark.md): question import and review, benchmark versions with development/holdout splits, publication checks, approval | `feat/mvp-04-benchmark` | Signed off 2026-10-18 |
| 4 | [Experiment](step-04-experiment.md): experiments with a live preview, submit with preflight and reservation, eval-lead approval, run manifests, baseline anchors | `feat/mvp-05-experiment` | Waiting for sign-off |
| 5 | [Execute](step-05-execute.md): runs from approved manifests, live capture within target limits, retries and attempts, cancel, deterministic scoring, baseline anchors; New snapshot fix | `feat/mvp-06-run` | Waiting for sign-off |
| 6 | Measure | not started | |
| 7 | Compare and diagnose | not started | |
| 8 | Review and qualify | not in MVP | |
| 9 | Release decision | not started | |

Every command in these files runs from the repo root.

## Judges (`src/judges.py`)

| Judge | What it checks | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| `regex_numeric` | Every number in the answer appears in the context | $0, <1 ms |
| `lexical_overlap` | Each answer sentence has >= 75% of its content words in the context | $0, <1 ms |
| `hhem_2.1_open` | Vectara HHEM-2.1-Open, P(consistent) >= 0.5; revision pinned; needs `trust_remote_code` | $0, CPU |
| `lettucedetect_base_v1` | LettuceDetect ModernBERT, flags unsupported answer spans; revision pinned | $0, CPU |

findings.text:
**Yes.** The harness builds 242 labelled cases from the reviewed benchmark,
runs 4 pluggable judges (968 calls, 0 failures), and reports qualification
metrics with clustered confidence intervals, broken down by error type.
Adding Ragas or DeepEval means writing one adapter class.

**No cheap judge qualifies** under the PRD rule (sensitivity and specificity
>= 0.90, lower bounds >= 0.80), alone or combined. The breakdown shows
exactly where each one fails, which is the information needed to decide what
the LLM judges must add.

## Results

Judges were scored on 242 cases (135 unsupported, 107 supported), with 95%
cluster-bootstrap intervals over the 53 questions.

| Judge | Sensitivity | Specificity | AUROC | Kappa | ms/case (CPU) | Qualifies |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| regex_numeric | 0.667 [0.58, 0.76] | 0.916 [0.86, 0.96] | 0.80 | 0.56 | 0.1 | no |
| lexical_overlap | 0.689 [0.61, 0.76] | 0.841 [0.77, 0.90] | 0.86 | 0.52 | 0.2 | no |
| HHEM-2.1-Open | **0.733** [0.67, 0.80] | 0.869 [0.80, 0.93] | **0.87** | 0.59 | 358 (p95 784) | no |
| LettuceDetect base | 0.681 [0.61, 0.76] | **0.944** [0.90, 0.98] | 0.82 | **0.60** | 603 (p95 1175) | no |

It anchors ground truth to source spans and shows where pipelines break.

scenes.subheading: Measure and govern RAG systems, then ship the workflow.

narration.text: The lifecycle spans project setup, corpus governance, benchmark approval, and execution.
The web app is a React and TypeScript shell over the API.
The FastAPI app loads the registry, builds storage, and mounts routers.
It refuses to start if the registry is invalid, which protects the platform.
Admin routes create users, update profiles, and reset passwords.
Each change is audited, so operator actions stay traceable.
Target adapters inject the idempotency key and attempt header automatically.
That keeps retries reproducible when the simulator or a real endpoint is called.
The bake-off scores 242 cases across four judges.
HHEM reaches 0.733 sensitivity, while LettuceDetect reaches 0.944 specificity.
You can run the simulator with uvicorn, then query it with curl.
For the bake-off, create a virtual environment and run the harness.
Clone the repository, start the stack, and explore the workflow.
Then try the simulator and the bake-off to see AEVIS in action.
